speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Having said that, over the years, as wages rise, more consumers can afford and are prepared to pay for higher-end meal options and operators have, therefore, responded to these trends.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have seen coffee shop menu items change, expand and increase in price points over time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government continuously pays attention to ground concerns about cost of living and recognise the need for our heartland coffee shops to maintain some lower-priced meals and drinks to cater to those who may not be able to spend as much on cooked food.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This would have been hard to achieve if we had continued to leave things entirely to market forces.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government, therefore, needed to intervene, but in a measured way that takes business sustainability into account.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Budget meals are full meals that are priced affordably, as compared to the average price of meals sold at nearby eating places.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Since 2018, all new HDB rental coffee shops that are tendered out to operators must provide budget meals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is done under the Price Quality Method tender framework, also known as the PQM tender framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Under this framework, operators were required to provide six budget meals as well as a budget drink.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I want to take this opportunity to thank Mr Louis Chua for affirming the PQM method.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I wish to clarify that HDB does not, as Mr Leong Mun Wai had suggested, require coffee shops to offer budget meals below market prices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The prices should be affordable, compared to surrounding options, but we do not require them to be lower.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This move coincided with a period of rising food and energy prices and sustained inflation caused by disruptions following the war in Ukraine and extreme weather.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We know that consumers view coffee shop prices as an everyday expenditure and are sensitive to across-the-board price increases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Hence, budget meals became relevant not just to lower-income groups but to everyone who cared about cost of living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are glad that the initiative has helped more families to stretch their household budget.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: At the same time, we are mindful of the need to strike a balance between residents' needs for affordable food options and the operators' and stallholders' business sustainability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Unlike what Mr Leong Mun Wai has asserted, we do not require every stall in an HDB-owned coffee shop to offer budget meals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Generally, an operator of an HDB rental coffee shop is required to provide four to six budget meals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This requirement can be met by different stalls in the coffee shop and it is also possible for there to be stalls within an HDB-owned coffee shop that do not participate in offering budget meals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Operators and stallholders have the flexibility to propose the budget meals that they wish to offer during the tender or tenancy renewal process and are at liberty to determine the prices of all other meals that they offer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are constantly engaging the industry and monitoring feedback from consumers as well as feedback from operators and stallholders and we are prepared to make adjustments to the scheme where necessary.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Last year, HDB and GovTech worked together to launch the BudgetMealGoWhere website to help residents locate HDB coffee shops offering budget meals more easily and conveniently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This website now includes listings of recommendations from the public, submitted through the Great Budget Meal Hunt, a related initiative which we launched earlier this year to crowdsource recommendations of budget meals in HDB coffee shops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In the past six months, 126 privately-owned HDB coffee shops have also started offering budget meals and drinks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Stalls in privately-owned HDB coffee shops that have voluntarily committed to provide budget meals will display the community budget meal decal in red and blue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HDB supports budget meal providers in several ways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The rebate starts as soon as the new requirements are in place and operators are required to pass on the rental discount to participating stall operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will intervene if stallholders tell us this did not happen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Also, at the same time, HDB has kept stable the rent it has been collecting from its coffee shops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We also stepped up efforts to raise publicity for these coffee shop operators and stalls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Not only do we want to raise awareness of the budget meals, but we also want to give recognition and generate interest so that more may visit these coffee shops and bring business to all stallholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: They are vibrant melting pots of diverse and affordable local food that tell stories of Singapore, how different cultures interweave into a unique heritage of who we are as a people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: They are community dining rooms where Singaporeans from all walks of life gather, socialise, interact over good food in an informal setting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Hawker centres are special and quite different from food courts and restaurants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our hawker centres are special because of the hawkers that make them come to life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: They are our community kitchens, where hawkers thrive as masters of their craft to serve comfort food beloved by Singaporeans and famous worldwide.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These hawkers often specialise in specific heritage dishes, such as Hainanese chicken rice, Nyonya laksa, nasi lemak or roti prata.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I know this is the time of the day when everyone gets hungry, but I just cannot help but mention some of these delicacies in our hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our hawkers work long hours, often more than 14 hours a day, especially on weekends and public holidays, to serve us our comfort food.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Many have dedicated their lives to perfecting specific dishes, often passing down skills, special recipes and cultural traditions from one generation to the next.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Each dish is unique to a particular hawker stall because it is infused with the special recipe and the master touch of the hawker.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The flavour of char kway teow from Hong Lim Park Hawker Centre is different from the one at Zion Riverside Food Centre and I like both of them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Yes, doctors do eat char kway teow as well, but I must say, please do it in moderation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These two char kway teows, they are my favourites and, I am sure, they each have their own hardcore supporters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Like many of you, I go to different hawker centres to savour the authentic differences in flavour, even of the same dish.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Each hawker centre has its own character and a different mix of food choices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is why we all have our own choice of favourite hawker dishes, even our own choice of favourite hawker centres and we often debate endlessly on which hawker centre has the best chicken rice or where we can find the best nasi lemak.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: While some hawkers have done well and opened stalls in other hawker centres, and some have even ventured out into the restaurant space, as noted by Mr Keith Chua, the vast majority of stalls at our hawker centres are generally run by stallholders themselves, who prepare each dish meticulously with their unique touches as it is ordered, and retain its individuality, unlike a franchise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, we can all agree that if a hawker centre becomes replaced by franchises, the texture and the nature of a hawker centre as we know it today, will be quite different.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Singaporeans and Members of this House across both sides of the aisle will agree with me, that this unique Singaporean institution must be nurtured, supported and protected to ensure that our hawker centres and hawkers can thrive for generations to come.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Some of our hawker heroes are gathered at the Gallery today – even at this time, some of them have stoically stayed on.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To keep this unique character of our hawker centres, our hawker policy will need to reflect three fundamental objectives and principles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These principles apply regardless of how we run our hawker centres, whether they are managed by NEA or by operators under our newer SEHC model.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I will address the different operating models later in my speech.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I listened to Mr Leong Mun Wai's speech and that of many other Members today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: No one will disagree with the three objectives I spelt out earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But in trying to achieve all three objectives at the same time, we must recognise that there are inherent tensions that, sometimes, pull in opposite directions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For instance, addressing consumers' desire for lower food prices can inadvertently run counter to our wish to support our hawkers in making a decent living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Without a decent income, it will be difficult to attract young Singaporeans, who have many career options, to enter this trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Similarly, allowing more foreigners to work in our hawker centres may alleviate cost and manpower concerns for our hawkers, but it could dilute our local hawker culture and identity, and change the feel and nature of our hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As such, there is a need to strike a balance between the interests of all parties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Singaporeans face cost-of-living pressures on many fronts, especially in recent years due to global inflation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Singaporeans are understandably concerned about how much they pay for food at our hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Hawkers, like all of us, also feel these pressures, as the cost of ingredients form a large part of their operating cost, as you have heard from some of the speakers earlier as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In pricing their food, many hawkers struggle between keeping food affordable for their loyal customers while trying to raise prices to cover the increases in ingredient and manpower costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is a struggle that many of us in the House, I believe, can empathise with.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I know that a good number of hawkers have kept their food prices unchanged over the years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: One of our hawkers is here with us today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Melvin Chew, who runs Jin Ji Teochew Braised Duck and Kway Chap at Chinatown Complex Market and Food Centre, shared with me recently, that he had maintained his food prices for over 20 years since the 2000s to offer $3 meals to his customers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: While he had previously considered raising prices, I understand he decided to maintain his $3 meals to benefit the older folks staying in the area.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It was only after the pandemic that he raised prices to $4 to cope with the rising business costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Another example is Mr Macheal s/o Aumeer Ali.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Macheal sells wanton noodles at Tanglin Halt Market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: He maintained his prices at $3.50 over five years to serve the seniors from Tanglin Halt Estate who form most of his clientele.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Only in late-2023 did he increase prices to $4, due to rising costs over the years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It is not easy for hawkers to earn a fair living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our hawkers are generally mindful of the profile of the customers they serve and they try their best to hold off any price increases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But hawkers need to be able to price their food realistically and adjust them from time to time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I echo the anecdote that Mr Edward Chia shared in his speech, about Mr Zuhairi who runs Project Penyek at Senja Hawker Centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The worries shared by Mr Zuhairi about the rising cost of just one ingredient, chilli, as well as ingredient wastage when customers prefer just to eat the different part of a chicken, may sound quite trivial for us who wonder why there is so much fuss about just a little bit of extra sambal or picking the part of the chicken that we order.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But these are the cost components that have a direct impact on a hawker's earnings, which are already not high to begin with.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Absorbing price increases of ingredients would effectively mean a pay cut for a hawker, on top of the already slim margins.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I am sure many Singaporeans can empathise with this, even as price increases are not always easy to accept for anyone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: There is another dimension to this, which is that hawkers inherently face limitations to how much they can sell and earn, because they operate the stalls themselves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Most do not sell as many meals or earn as much per portion of food they sell.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This low income is also a point noted by Mr Leong Mun Wai earlier in his speech.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Like everyone, our hawkers need an income that is sustainable over time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This has implications for the sustainability of the hawker trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As our ageing hawkers gradually retire, we will need new blood to sustain the hawker trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: At present, fortunately nearly all of our cooked food stalls are occupied.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But if hawkers cannot make a decent livelihood, the hawker trade would become much less attractive to our younger generation who have many more career options.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is a point also noted by Mr Louis Chua earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Another tension arises as we try to help hawkers manage their manpower costs while we seek to preserve the "local" identity of our hawker culture and heritage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our policy of only allowing Singaporeans and PRs to be stallholders at hawker centres serves to safeguard this precious aspect of our Singaporean identity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I recognise that our hawkers face the practical challenge of hiring non-locals to ease manpower constraints.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But a full liberalisation for foreign manpower may alter the nature of our hawker centres significantly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, these are competing tensions and there are, unfortunately, no easy solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our recent moves seek to strike a careful balance, by allowing more LTVP or LTVP+ holders – who have nexus and ties to Singaporean families – to be stall assistants, which would hopefully help in some way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Government fully acknowledges the impact of global inflation on the affordability of hawker food and the livelihoods of hawkers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We know the difficult operating environment and challenges our hawkers face, as well as Singaporeans' desire for affordable hawker food.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These are difficult tensions to balance and there is no simple solution or easy fix.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We agree with Mr Leong Mun Wai that the Government has a role to play in supporting our hawkers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: That is what the Government has been doing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For decades now, since we gathered itinerant street hawkers into our hawker centres and, through our policies, sought to provide hawkers with a conducive operating environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As we have restarted building hawker centres from 2011, we set out to better address the needs of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In so doing, we also set out with a forward-looking mindset to test and explore new models that would allow us to safeguard hawker livelihoods and consumers' needs, while keeping our hawker centre landscape responsive to an evolving operating context.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I will explain more about the SEHC model later.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We need to find a way, as a society, to keep hawker fare affordable, while ensuring that hawkers can earn a fair living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Underpinning this solution must be a strong social compact that brings all stakeholders together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Government foots the cost of building hawker centres and sets policies to support our hawkers and provide them with a conducive operating environment, to ensure that they are able to provide Singaporeans with affordable food at our hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The local community and private sector have a role in driving ground-up initiatives to support both hawkers and patrons and we heard many examples earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Consumers can support our hawkers by patronising them and being prepared to pay a fair price for hawker food to uplift the livelihoods of our hawkers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Government has implemented policies to support our hawkers by providing a conducive operating environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We review these policies regularly to ensure that they are aligned with operating realities on the ground and for hawker centres to serve the needs of both hawkers and consumers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We recognise the cost pressures that hawkers face.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Leong Mun Wai also acknowledges that rent is not a major cost component in his speech earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: While Government does not regulate hawker food prices, NEA has measures in place to provide a conducive operating environment for hawkers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: First, on manpower costs, we have been paying close attention to two aspects: improving access to manpower and improving hawkers' productivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The income of hawkers is very much dependent on how many meals they can serve a day, especially during peak hours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: There is only so much that one pair of hands can do.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We understand hawkers' challenges in hiring stall assistants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is something we need to balance with safeguarding the local identity of our hawker culture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We do so by ensuring that being a stallholder at NEA's hawker centres remains reserved for Singapore Citizens and PRs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In doing so, we also ensure low barriers to entry for Singaporeans who wish to enter the F&B business through the hawker trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In Mr Leong Mun Wai and Mr Louis Chua's speeches earlier, they suggested allowing one Work Permit holder per stall to work as stall assistants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The suggestion is not inconceivable actually and there are real needs that the hawkers face in sourcing for manpower.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But there are differences between hawker centres and other food establishments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Private coffee shops and F&B establishments operate like SMEs, so they are subjected to the usual quota system that MOM applies to all operating businesses here in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our hawker centres, on the other hand, are an integral part of our cultural heritage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: They are unique and their local nature is something we want to preserve, which is why we thought very carefully about making such moves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is why we calibrate any relaxation on restrictions on who can work at our hawker centres very carefully.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As I have said earlier, full liberalisation of manpower in hawker centres would significantly alter the makeup and the feel of these centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: There is really no science to this question.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It is really about what we are all prepared to accept as a society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Are we prepared to accept that the hawker centre that we are familiar with changes in nature to something quite different?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, I think this is something that will probably have to evolve over time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: If Members recall, in the early 2010s, there was significant concern among Singaporeans about seeing more foreigners working in hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: And this very issue was raised in this House, which Mr Edward Chia has earlier on also shared with Members what transpired in Parliament in 2010.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As some Singaporeans may still not be able to accept seeing a significant alteration in a make-up of hawker centres, we will adjust and evolve our policies to take these views into account.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is one example of how we continually review and adjust our policies to adjust to changing circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But the reality is that each additional headcount is an added cost to our hawkers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, a more sustainable approach to manpower is to make every person more productive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Therefore, NEA has implemented measures to support hawkers in enhancing their productivity, which can help lighten the pressures of their manpower constraints.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: A key business cost hawkers deal with is raw materials.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Ms Hazel Poa raised the suggestion on centralised procurement to moderate such costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I believe in an earlier Parliamentary Sitting, Mr Melvin Yong did raise one of these suggestions in a PQ.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This centralised procurement idea is already present at some SEHCs, where operators have tapped on their network in the F&B and food supply sectors to offer bulk purchasing services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: With such services, their stallholders have the option to secure preferential rates for raw ingredients.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So far, the uptake among stallholders has not been widespread as most already have established relationships with their existing suppliers or are quite particular about the source and quality of the ingredients.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Remember what I said earlier about the unique nature of our hawker centres is that each stall is run by the hawkers themselves, with unique recipes and special touches.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Everyone has something they want to put as special to differentiate themselves from their competitors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Nonetheless, we will continue to support such initiatives where it benefits our hawkers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Apart from manpower, the Government has also implemented measures to ensure reasonable rent for hawkers and to address concerns on rent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: By keeping rent affordable, we can help make the cost of doing business lower for our hawkers, even if it is not by a large percentage, because rent is less than 10% of the operating cost.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Generally, stall rentals at hawker centres are lower than nearby eating establishments, such as coffee shops, food courts and small eateries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This has been the case even while overall prices have continued to rise over the decade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This also means, therefore, that the rent is now a smaller component of their costs compared to 10 years ago.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Government also extends generous subsidies to a segment of our Pioneer hawkers, who make up around 30% of cooked food stallholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For them, the rent is heavily subsidised at about $300 per month and this can be transferred to the immediate family members of the pioneer hawkers at the same low rent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I believe Mr Melvin Chew whom I spoke about earlier is also a beneficiary of this legacy system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Government builds hawker centres and does not use rent for cost recovery.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The rents are, in fact, determined by what the tenderer bids for and can be as low as $1.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The PSP and Mr Louis Chua raised the issue of rent and the bidding system for stall rentals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our policy is for non-subsidised stalls in NEA-managed hawker centres to be allocated via a tender system in which the stalls are tendered to the highest bidder, who pays the bid price for the first tenancy period of three years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This process is open, transparent and straightforward for prospective hawkers to understand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: A bidding system enables market mechanisms to work at hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The process encourages prospective hawkers that are committed and serious to come forward and submit a bid.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Before doing so, prospective hawkers would have to take into account the operating realities, business costs and decide on what kind of food they wish to sell.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: They know that what they bid will be what they have to pay.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Once the stall is opened, consumers will decide.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The quality and the price of the food will determine how well the stall will fare and how sustainable the stall will be.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This market mechanism has helped to shape our current hawker centre landscape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It is responsive to consumers' demands and changing expectations for hawker food, and it is fair for both hawkers and consumers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Those who can offer tasty meals that consumers feel are value for money will continue to do well, while those who are priced too high and do not meet consumers' taste expectations will eventually exit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This works in tandem with other measures by the Government to moderate hawker stall rents, which we regularly review and improve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Today, there is no reserve rent or minimum bid price.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This enables bidders to obtain stalls at low rental rates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: A few in 2023 and 2024 even won bids with rents as low as $1.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: There are stalls which are going at $1 bid price.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We saw that subletting of stalls led to higher rents in the past.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, we moved in 2012 to disallow such subletting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: After the first tenancy period of three years, rental is adjusted towards the Assessed Market Rent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We recently reviewed and changed this policy to stagger the downward adjustment of tendered rent over a longer period, in fact, over two tenancy renewals instead of one.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This will also discourage prospective hawkers from putting in excessively high tender bids.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It is not a perfect system, but collectively, our rental policies at NEA-managed hawker centres have served us reasonably well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, our system has actually kept rental prices reasonably affordable; in fact, a good number below the Assessed Market Rent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We have made recent changes and we expect to see some positive impact.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will continue to review, taking in suggestions and feedback from Members and from hawkers themselves to continue improving the system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: There are many views on the current price tender system model and what might be a better alternative that could replace it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Even the PSP itself has different views and proposed different options as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For example, Mr Leong Mun Wai suggested one method based on percentage of gross turnover with a base rent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But this will require a point-of-sale system for every stall in order to be able to track what the takings really are.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Ms Hazel Poa also proposed that we abandon the tender system and change it to a balloting one.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: She also suggested perhaps a fixed rent model as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As Mr Keith Chua noted, there really would not be a perfect system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For example, we also started to do the price quality method at our SEHC models where rent is pre-determined and stalls are awarded by the operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, we are open to trying different methods and see what works best.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I remember Mr Melvin Yong asking me in a PQ before, probably just about a couple of months ago.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This may not be fair to prospective tenderers with a genuine intent to set up a new stall because they will see their chances dwindle as more people come in and crowd into that space for a limited number of stalls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: And such a situation will not benefit patrons as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Ms Poa also suggested a fixed rent model to keep rental costs under control.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But the question we must ask is: what price will we use to predetermine the rent?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Let us just say we use the assessed market rent, which is professionally determined by valuers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Then, in that case, all prospective hawkers will end up paying this price.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But under today's system, as you heard me say earlier, the tendered rent for about 44% of stalls is actually below the Assessed Market Rent, based on our 2023 data.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In fact, as I said earlier, 20% pay less than $500.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Louis Chua also proposes a rental cap.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I thought it is useful for us to understand how a rental cap could distort the market dynamics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: If we set any cap threshold, we give the bidders the assurance that the bids will not go beyond a maximum ceiling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, that is the upside of a rental cap.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: However, doing so could also encourage bidders to bid more competitively towards that threshold in order to outprice the competition to secure the stall.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, that could well mean the end of the $1 bid stalls that we have in the system today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This could in turn lead to overall bid prices trending higher and the whole allocation system will no longer be fair and meaningful.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Even at less popular centres, the rental cap may also have an unintended consequence by inadvertently setting a price point that drive lower rentals upward toward the cap, as I have explained.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Louis Chua also proposes the Government take back control of all hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In fact, today, the Government already oversees all hawker centres and we have been able to achieve reasonable rents and conducive environment for hawkers through our policies for ensuring accessible and affordable food options.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Government has been responding to evolving needs and at different points in time, we have tried different management models in order to bring benefit to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: While our systems are not perfect, we have worked in partnership with our hawkers and operators to address these.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will continue to listen and engage, and fine-tune what needs to be improved.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I must also say that we should allow some space for the private sector to thrive in this space so there is a diversity of options for both hawkers and consumers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Some hawkers eventually do venture out to other F&B spaces to scale and grow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, I think we should not do it in a way that actually squeezes out the room for private sector to also be able to thrive in the scene.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: At the end of the day, we must ensure that whatever we do is transparent, easily understood by the tenderers and will lead to better outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We must make sure that the cure that we are all proposing is not going to be worse-off than the issue we are trying to resolve, to the detriment of hawkers and consumers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As Mr Leong has also noted, rent is not really the major cost factor.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: What hawkers need is customers footfall and fair pricing so that they can have a decent margin and an income on the goods that they sell.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Because even if the rent is free, no footfall equals to no income.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, we have to be quite clear that rent being a small component is not going to be the one that will make our hawkers fare better.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We continue to monitor the trends closely, as well as the attention that hawker stall rent has attracted recently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: A small percentage of bids can be quite high, especially at popular hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For example, the recent bid for a stall at Marine Parade Central Food Centre that Members have mentioned.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I must say that this outlier bid is the only one at that level of $10,000 in the last five years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This means that these people are still in the first tenancy term, because at the end of the third year, this 4% that is above the Assessed Market Rent on today's policy, will revert to the Assessed Market Rent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, we have to be quite careful not to abandon a system that has actually worked quite well and benefited many hawkers, just because of a small number of outliers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: There may be situations where prospective tenderers put in overly high bids upfront to secure their preferred stall, expecting their rents to be adjusted downwards to Assessed Market Rent after the first three years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Such bids may not be realistic and may distort prices over time, if they proliferate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, while the numbers, as I said, are small today, other tenderers could be disadvantaged from entering the hawker trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: First and quite important, we will make available more information and online business cost estimation tools.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We are introducing this to assist and encourage tenderers to make a more informed decision and to bid realistically, when they submit a tender bid for a hawker stall.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We are working on the details, which we plan to make public early next year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Doing so serves to deter prospective hawkers from submitting unrealistic bids.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I want to assure existing stallholders that you will not be affected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Of course, we recognise this is not a cure-all and tenderers could still submit high bids, if they assess that they have a viable business model with that bid.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Nonetheless, we hope that these changes will work hand-in-hand to encourage prospective hawkers to bid in a more considered and realistic manner moving forward.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will continue to monitor the tender bidding behaviours closely and review our tenancy policies from time to time to ensure that they stay relevant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I would now like to turn to the issue of operating models.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But before I do so, allow me to reiterate that regardless of how we manage our hawker centres, whether it is by NEA, or operators appointed under our SEHC model, our fundamental principles remain the same – hawkers and consumers remain at the heart of our policies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: There have been many comments about the SEHC model by Members today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In 2011, when we restarted building hawker centres, this was with Singaporeans in mind, to meet the community’s rising needs for access to a variety of food options at affordable prices, especially in areas under-served with F&B options.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We also needed to set up our new centres for success.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This meant exploring new models and being open to different approaches that would allow us to achieve our objectives to safeguard hawker livelihoods and consumers’ needs, while adapting to an evolving operating context far different from when we first started building hawker centres to resettle street hawkers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Foremost on our minds was to ensure that our new centres would be vibrant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Vibrancy is important not just to hawkers but consumers as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: There was a time when residents were unhappy that hawker centres were not opening long enough to serve their dining needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In fact, this issue was raised before and debated in Parliament too, back in the 2000s.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In recent years, we have also received feedback from residents and the community about operating hours for hawker centres and the need to ensure they are vibrant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In short, managing hawker centres can be a complex undertaking.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Hawker centres need to be vibrant with good visitorship and footfall.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: They need to provide a diverse food mix that responds to the evolving needs of changing demographics and be adaptable, and set up with the necessary conditions to be viable and sustainable for the long term.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: All these require the right business acumens to put together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Government agencies do not have the abilities or instincts to operate businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is the context for developing the SEHC model.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We assessed the SEHC model to have various benefits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: First, SEHC operators possess industry knowledge and experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: They can leverage their expertise in F&B and stall management to ensure the vibrancy of new centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Indeed, many have done so by developing a variety of localised programmes, including initiatives tailored to the community to drive visitorship and incubation programmes to provide business advice and support to aspiring hawkers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Second, SEHC operators can leverage their F&B networks to curate food mix and support stallholders to fine-tune their menu, such as through food tastings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This supports both hawkers and consumers, allowing the hawker centres to feature food that meet patrons’ expectations, which in turn supports hawkers’ businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Third, SEHC operators can introduce new and innovative practices to support stallholders in navigating changing operating contexts and industry developments, such as onboarding onto digital and online ordering platforms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This helps our hawker centres evolve and keep up with trends.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Good curation and visitorship are important ingredients for a vibrant hawker centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These allow hawkers to thrive and earn a fair livelihood.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In turn, when hawkers find it viable to operate stalls for longer hours, a centre can better meet the dining needs of the residents and community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These are the objectives that had to be met – and we believe can be met – by the SEHC management model.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As with any models, there will be operational issues that we need to continuously calibrate and make adjustments from time to time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will continue to engage SEHC operators and hawkers to make necessary changes, as and when needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In developing the model, we sought to strike a balance between ensuring: patrons’ needs for a hawker centre are met, including access to affordable food options and meals across the day; and hawkers' needs for a conducive operating environment to make a reasonable livelihood.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, the cost of operating an SEHC is partially borne by the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We have safeguards in place to ensure that operators do not profiteer and are expected to work closely with NEA as well as hawkers, to consider the interests and needs of both hawkers and residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In Mr Leong Mun Wai's speech earlier, he claimed that the operator of Jurong West Hawker Centre, JW50 Hawker Heritage, paid $4.86 million to Government to manage Jurong West Hawker Centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, they do not pay us $4.86 million.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In fact, NEA pays this to JW50 over a span of nine years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, as you can see, this is at a significant cost that is borne by Government over time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As you heard from Mr Ang Wei Neng earlier, when he shared about the Jurong West Hawker Centre, the hawkers who are there pay about $1,000-plus for rental, which is quite similar to what other hawkers in NEA-managed hawker centres also pay.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This kind of management model is also not the kind of business environment for hawkers that you could find in many other cities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Leong gave the example of New York city.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I believe that Mr KF Seetoh will be very familiar with the kind of high rental and labour costs that are faced by hawkers, given his experience with Urban Hawker in New York.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I think Members who are interested can Google Mothership – there are quite a few articles written about this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I think Mr Edward Chia had shared earlier that some hawkers that are operating in New York face high rental costs, operating costs, ingredient costs, manpower costs and some of them have actually exited as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is an illustration of how through our investment in hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Through our various policies, we have tried to keep costs low and manageable for hawkers here, so they can continue to thrive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: When submitting tender proposals, prospective SEHC operators must also include their proposed stall rentals and other operating costs that would be charged to stallholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To provide stability for stallholders, upon award of the tender, operators are not allowed to vary hawkers’ rent and other operating charges over the tenancy term and must keep costs transparent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This helps new stallholders coming into these new centres manage operating costs as they build their clientele, while the centre gradually establishes itself.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Second, to ensure fair operating conditions for hawkers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Such conditions are part of the tenancy agreements between the SEHC operators and the stallholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The operators put in place the necessary conditions to account for the needs of the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For example, operating hours specify that stallholders must open their stalls for a specific number of days and hours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This serves to ensure that centres would be vibrant and have sufficient stalls in operation to serve meals for residents throughout the day.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Nevertheless, conditions are also in place to take care of the well-being of our hawkers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: NEA provided guidelines on the terms of such tenancy agreements, including on termination clauses, liquidated damages clauses and operating hours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For instance, on operating hours, stallholders are not required to work more than five days a week or eight hours a day.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These are guidelines that operators need to comply with before using their tenancy agreements with stallholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Operators are also required to explain the tenancy agreement to stallholders in simple terms for the stallholders' understanding, before they sign it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Once again, there is a fine balance needed to look after the interests of both our hawkers and our community, for whom hawker centres are built for.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: You can imagine that SEHC operators may generate operating surpluses in some years and incur losses in some other years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But when surpluses are available, operators have run initiatives to raise footfall and business levels to benefit stallholders, such as providing shuttle bus services at Yishun Park Hawker Centre and organising festive events at Bukit Canberra Hawker Centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Some operators have also tapped on their surpluses to help the stallholders reduce their operating costs, such as for cleaning.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Also, SEHC operators, as part of their tender proposals, must propose ways to ensure affordable food options are available.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It is for the SEHC operators to propose and set a price.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It is not for NEA to dictate what is a reasonable price.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is not an attempt to force hawkers to sell all of their dishes at low prices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Instead, the intent is for operators to work with hawkers to offer a range of food offerings at different price points.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Hawkers therefore still retain flexibility to offer other food items and sell them at appropriate prices, so that they can continue to earn an overall fair living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Hawkers are not expected to make a loss selling value meals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: SEHC operators can propose to revise the price of such value meals options, which NEA will review based on the market situation and the stallholders’ ability to make a fair livelihood.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This has, in fact, been done before, at Ci Yuan Hawker Centre, where the price has been reviewed and adjusted, based on feedback from operators and hawkers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: NEA remains open to consider other suggestions that operators may propose, based on their viability and feasibility to ensure that sufficient affordable options are provided at the SEHCs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: SEHC operators must also engage hawkers through regular Hawker Feedback Group sessions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These are held at least once every quarter, where operators gather feedback and ideas from their stallholders to improve the hawker centres and the hawkers’ livelihoods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: NEA has worked closely with hawkers and operators as well as other stakeholders to refine the SEHC model over the years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will continue to listen to concerns and input to evolve and improve the model as we go along.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our SEHCs have brought overall benefits to hawkers and patrons alike, and are well-established within their communities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: SEHC operators have curated food stalls in their SEHCs to ensure good quality and variety, and kept their centres open for all three meals to meet patrons’ dining needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Average occupancy at SEHCs remains high with low stall turnover, comparable to NEA-managed centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: While the comparison in termination numbers at SEHCs as compared to NEA-managed hawker centres cited by Mr Leong are factual – he said about 8% versus 3% – they do need to be put into context.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The average termination rate cited for SEHCs, which is the 8% cited by Mr Leong, also accounted for new SEHCs that have just opened and are starting out.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: During this period, new centres tend to have some attrition and this is a natural part of business volatility.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: When businesses at new SEHCs move into a steady state, stall termination tend to stabilise and in fact, are no different compared to NEA-managed hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: There continues to be high interest in applying for stalls at SEHCs, such as those recently opened at Anchorvale, Buangkok and Woodleigh.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Also, SEHCs have performed better in cleanliness, centre management and place-making activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Operating costs for stallholders at SEHCs, including rentals, remain manageable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: When comparing rental, it should not just be based on absolute rental, but one should also consider aspects such as stall size and amenities in the centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Nonetheless, we do not take all this for granted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We also recognise that some operators have done better while others have faced implementation challenges along the way, especially when they first get started.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is also why we renew the management of SEHCs via an open tender after the incumbent operators’ final tenancy term.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It is a transparent process that allows incumbents that have done well to be considered favourably, while weeding out poorer-performing operators if necessary.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Such a system enables healthy competition between the SEHC operators and motivates them to refine and improve their management models over time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As we roll out the SEHC model to more new hawker centres, we will continue to monitor the implementation of the SEHC model closely and work with hawkers and operators to ensure that our new hawker centres continue to serve the interests of patrons well and ensure the well-being of our hawkers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Next, I will address the concerns raised about the affordability of food at hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Today, our hawker centres across our island continue to provide the most affordable cooked food options for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: That is why we often receive requests from residents to have a hawker centre in their neighbourhoods, even when it is already well served by other F&B outlets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As MPs on the ground, we often get such requests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our key focus therefore must be to ensure a sufficient supply of hawker stalls to cater to residents in all regions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We are committed to doing so and we will continue maintaining our existing hawker centres as we as we build new ones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This would result in an unsustainable hawker trade, discourage new hawkers from joining the trade and would eventually affect everyone if affordable hawker food becomes less available.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It is not prudent in the long run and hawkers would bear the brunt while also experiencing the same cost-of-living pressures just like everyone else.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We have to be careful about over-regulating across the board.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Broadly speaking, market competition is an important self-regulating force for hawker food prices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We have been talking about affordable food, but “affordable” might not necessarily equate to “cheap”.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As I mentioned earlier in my speech, hawkers consider various factors when pricing their food, including operating costs and the need to remain competitive with other stalls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I have spoken to hawkers, a young hawker, one of them, Darren, who shared that many of them practise what he would say “honest pricing”, in which they price their food to reflect the true cost and quality of ingredients, and apply a reasonable but modest profit margin to sustain their livelihood.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Hawkers know that consumers are discerning and they need to be honest with their pricing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In allowing the market to function, another hawker, Mr Noorman from Nasi Lemak Ayam Taliwang, I think he is there in the gallery as well, he said, "We can let our hawkers and their customers find the right balance of where the price point for hawker food should be".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: And over time, this enables a sustainable hawker centre landscape that is responsive to both hawkers’ and consumers’ needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To help Singaporeans cope with cost-of-living concerns, you heard from Senior Parliamentary Secretary Shawn Huang earlier that the Government has introduced broad-based measures such as providing CDC Vouchers under the enhanced Assurance Package.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I am heartened to hear from Mr Edward Chia’s speech that hawkers at Senja Hawker Centre shared that these CDC Vouchers have contributed directly to their revenue and brought in new customers for their businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I am also heartened that many businesses and community groups are also stepping up and doing their part to help Singaporeans and hawkers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Various MPs also shared their local initiatives, but I will just share maybe a couple more.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In 2023, the Marine Parade Citizens’ Consultative Committee, the Marine Parade Merchant’s Association and Katong Joo Chiat Business Association worked together with some hawkers in three hawker centres and coffee shops to launch a Value Meal@Marine Parade initiative for patrons.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In September 2024, the Marine Parade constituency also launched the Marine Parade Family Vouchers for eligible families to use at its neighbourhood merchants, markets and hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These are measures, ground-up activities that also go to help both those in need and the hawkers themselves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The private sector has also introduced similar initiatives, and you heard from Mr Chia earlier, for example, DBS’ ongoing Support Our Heartlands initiative and their earlier "5 Million Hawker Meals" scheme that was shared.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I am deeply encouraged by these initiatives which support our hawkers and the broader community, and I hope to see many more of them as we continue to uplift and safeguard our hawker culture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I agree with Mr Leong, that to safeguard our hawker trade for future generations, one of our key priorities is to nurture a new generation of young hawkers to take over the reins.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To attract more Singaporeans to join the hawker trade, we need to first ensure that hawkers are able to earn a fair living, work in a clean and comfortable environment, and receive the support that they require.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These underpin our policies, as I have mentioned earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Leong and Mr Louis Chua proposed setting up a hawker academy to be a focal point for training young aspiring hawkers in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In fact, we already have a similar academy in place.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Under our current Hawkers Development Programme, NEA and SkillsFuture Singapore appoints the Asian Culinary Institute under Nanyang Polytechnic to provide training to aspiring hawkers and equip them with the necessary skills for their businesses, such as business strategy and business pricing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, that concept is already in action today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We are encouraged to see aspiring hawkers enter the trade through these means, with some choosing to preserve traditional recipes, while others infuse new, creative and innovative ideas to modernise hawker fare.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This diversity contributes to the richness and depth of our evolving hawker culture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Furthermore, SEHC operators also run various incubation programmes to support their stallholders to ease into the hawker trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: After all, it is in their interest to make sure that the hawkers succeed in their centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For example, Fei Siong Social Enterprise Pte Ltd introduced the Entrepreneurship Programme at Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The programme provides mentorship and support for young hawkerpreneurs in areas such as culinary skills, stall set-up, menu creation and marketing activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Fei Siong also provided financial assistance, such as purchasing cooking equipment at interest-free instalments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Collectively, the programmes by NEA and SEHC operators have helped to inject younger entrants into the hawker scene.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will continue to review the programme outcomes and identify other areas to better encourage and support aspiring hawkers to enter and stay in the hawker trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Leong proposed that hawker centre management be taken over by a new Government agency to be called Hawker Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Therefore, what he is proposing is a re-organisation of an existing dedicated team that is already functioning.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But what is more important is that whatever entity that oversees the management of hawker centres should be plugged in to the day-to-day concerns of individual centres and be responsive to its evolving needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is what our place managers does on a day-to-day basis, and our SEHC operators are also able to do this, too.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: NEA works closely with hawkers, as well as industry associations, like the Federation of Merchant Associations of Singapore, and we assign place managers to each hawker centre so that the nexus is tight.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I turn back now to the Motion that is being debated today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For Singaporeans, having to pay 50 cents or a dollar more for hawker meals could feel like a dent in their wallets, as prices of other daily essentials also add up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As the Government, and with the support of our local community and the private sector, we are doing what we can to mitigate the impact of these rising costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I want to thank Members who have acknowledged the practical realities we operate in and for reaffirming the Government's efforts to do right by our hawkers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: At the heart of the debate today is how we can sustain and grow our invaluable hawker culture so that it continues to thrive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is something that the Government is fully committed to do.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
