text: But we must recognise that there are often competing objectives and, as consumers, we can all play an important role in this, too.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Many Singaporeans are worried about the impact of global inflationary pressures on the cost of living, and understandably so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: However, for hawkers to earn a fair living, they need to price food realistically.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: While price increases are not always easy to accept, we must remember that how much a hawker can sell a bowl of rice or noodles for is dependent on how much Singaporeans are prepared to pay.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We must form a strong social compact to ensure that our hawker culture can continue to thrive and Singaporeans can continue to enjoy hawker fare for many more generations to come.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We all want our hawker centres and hawker culture to continue to thrive, but it entails a fine balancing act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This would not have been possible without the readiness and commitment from our hawkers and hawker associations to work with the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We may not always get this right the first time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: With your inputs and feedback, and as circumstances change, we will review and adjust our policies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We have done so in the past and we will continue to fine-tune and improve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: What is important in all of these adjustments is that our hawkers must be able to earn a fair livelihood.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is critical for our hawker culture to thrive for a long time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Without our hawkers as torchbearers, our hawker centres will be empty and our hawker culture will disappear.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The year 2025 will be our 60th year as an independent country.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It will also mark the fifth anniversary since the UNESCO inscription for hawker culture in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Hawkers have always played an integral role in building our country and hawker culture has been an important part of our national Singaporean identity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To Members of this House and to all Singaporeans, I want to assure you that safeguarding our hawker culture remains an important priority for this Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We are committed to work together with our hawker community and our stakeholders to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Together, we can sustain our hawker culture to thrive for generations to come.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, our hawker centres are an integral part of Singaporeans' daily lives and our cultural identity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: They are vibrant melting pots of diverse and affordable local food that tell stories of Singapore – how different cultures interweave into a unique heritage of who we are as a people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: They are community dining rooms, where Singaporeans from all walks of life gather, socialise and interact over good food in an informal setting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Hawker centres are special and quite different from food courts and restaurants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our hawker centres are special because of the hawkers that make them come to life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: They are our community kitchens where hawkers thrive as masters of their craft to serve comfort food beloved by Singaporeans and known worldwide.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These hawkers often specialise in specific local dishes such as Hainanese chicken rice, nasi lemak, Nyonya laksa or roti prata.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: They work long hours, often more than 14 hours a day especially on weekends and public holidays to serve us our comfort food.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Many have dedicated their lives to perfecting specific dishes, often passing down skills, recipes and cultural traditions from one generation to the next.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Each dish is unique to a particular hawker stall.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The flavor of char kway teow from Hong Lim Park Hawker Centre is different from the one at Zion Riverside Food Centre and I like both of them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: They are my favorites and they each have their own die-hard followers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Like many of you, I go to different hawker centres to savour the authentic differences of the same dish.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Each hawker centre has its own character and a different mix of food choices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is why we all have our own choice of favorite hawker dishes and often debate endlessly on which hawker centre has the best chicken rice and where the best nasi lemak can be found.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: While some hawkers have done well and opened stalls in other hawker centres, and some have even ventured out into the restaurant space, the vast majority of stalls at our hawker centres are generally run by stallholders themselves, preparing each meal with their unique touches as it is ordered and retaining its individuality, unlike a franchise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I think Singaporeans and Members across both sides of the aisle will agree, that this unique Singaporean institution must be nurtured, supported and protected, to ensure that our hawker centres and hawkers can thrive for generations to come.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Some of our hawker heroes are gathered at the gallery today – I would like to show appreciation to their contributions and welcome and thank them for coming down today as we discuss this important issue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I think no one will disagree with these objectives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But in trying to achieve all three objectives at the same time, we must recognise that there are inherent tensions that sometimes pull in opposite directions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For instance, addressing consumers’ desire for lower food prices can inadvertently run counter to our wish to support our hawkers in making a decent living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Without a decent income, it will be difficult to attract young Singaporeans who have many career options to enter this trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Similarly, allowing more foreigners to work in our hawker centres may alleviate cost and manpower concerns for our hawkers, but it could dilute our local hawker culture and identity and change the feel of our hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As such, there is a need to strike a balance between the interests of all parties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Singaporeans face cost-of-living pressures on many fronts, especially in recent years due to global inflation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Global food prices have been volatile in recent years due to supply chain disruptions resulting from climate change and geopolitical events.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We feel this impact keenly because Singapore imports over 90% of our food.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Singaporeans are understandably concerned about how much they pay for food at our hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In pricing their food, many hawkers struggle between keeping food affordable for their loyal customers while having to raise prices to cover the increases in ingredient and manpower costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is a struggle that many of us in the House empathise with.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I know that a good number of hawkers have kept their food prices unchanged over the years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: One of our hawkers, Mr Melvin Chew, who runs Jin Ji Teochew Braised Duck and Kway Chap at Chinatown Complex Market and Food Centre, shared with me that he had maintained his food prices for over 20 years since the 2000s to offer $3 duck rice to customers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I understand he tried to maintain his $3 meals to benefit the older folks staying in the area.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It was only after the pandemic that he raised prices to $4 to cope with rising business costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It is not easy for hawkers to earn a fair living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our hawkers are generally mindful of the profile of the customers they serve and they try their best to hold off raising prices of their food.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But hawkers need to be able to price their food realistically and adjust them from time to time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Absorbing price increases of ingredients would effectively mean a pay cut for a hawker, on top of slim profit margins.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I am sure many Singaporeans can empathise with this, even as price increases are not always easy to accept.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: There is another dimension to this, which is that hawkers inherently face limitations to how much they can sell and earn, because they operate the stall themselves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Most do not sell as many meals or earn as much per meal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As Mr Edward Chia’s example has highlighted, many hawkers barely make a 30-cent or 40-cent margin per meal they sell.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Like everyone, our hawkers need an income that is sustainable over time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This has implications for the sustainability of the hawker trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As our ageing hawkers gradually retire, we will need new blood to sustain the hawker trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But if hawkers cannot make a decent livelihood, the hawker trade would become much less attractive to our younger generation who have many more career options.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Another tension arises as we try to help hawkers manage their manpower costs while we seek to preserve the “local” identity of our hawker culture and heritage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our policy of only allowing Singaporeans and PRs to be stallholders at hawker centres serves to safeguard this precious aspect of our Singaporean identity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I recognise that our hawkers face the practical challenge of hiring non-locals to ease manpower constraints.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But a full liberalisation for foreign manpower may alter the nature of our hawker centres significantly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These are competing tensions and there are no easy solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We know the difficult operating environment and challenges our hawkers face, as well as Singaporeans’ desire for affordable hawker food.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: And there is no simple solution or easy fix.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We agree with Mr Leong that the Government has a role to play in supporting our hawkers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: That is what the Government has been doing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For decades now, since we gathered itinerant street hawkers into our hawker centres, and, through our policies, sought to provide hawkers with a conducive operating environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: And as we restarted building hawker centres from 2011, we set out to better address the needs of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In so doing, we also set out with a forward-looking mindset to test and explore new models that would allow us to safeguard hawker livelihoods and consumers’ needs, while keeping our hawker centre landscape responsive to an evolving operating context.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I will explain more about the SEHC model later.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We need to find a way as a society to keep hawker fare affordable, while ensuring that hawkers can earn a fair living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Underpinning this solution must be a strong social compact that brings all stakeholders together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Government foots the cost of building hawker centres and sets policies to support our hawkers and provide them with a conducive operating environment, to ensure that they are able to provide Singaporeans with affordable food at our hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The local community and private sector have a role in driving ground-up initiatives to support both hawkers and patrons and consumers can support our hawkers by patronising them and being prepared to pay a fair price for hawker food to uplift the livelihoods of our hawkers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The rents are determined by what the tenderer bids for.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This process is open, transparent and straightforward for prospective hawkers to understand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: A bidding system enables market mechanisms to work at hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The process encourages prospective hawkers that are committed and serious to come forward and submit a bid.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Before doing so, prospective hawkers have to take into account operating realities and business costs and decide on what food they wish to sell.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Once a stall is open, consumers will decide.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The quality and price of food will determine how well the stall fares and how sustainable the stall will be.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This market mechanism has helped to shape our current hawker centre landscape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It is responsive to consumers’ demands and changing expectations for hawker food, and fair for both hawkers and consumers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This works in tandem with other measures by the Government to moderate hawker stall rents, which we regularly review and improve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Today, there is no reserve rent or minimum bid prices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This enables bidders to obtain stalls at low rental rates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: After the first tenancy period of three years, rental is adjusted towards the Assessed Market Rate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We recently reviewed and changed this policy to stagger the downward adjustment of tendered rent over a longer period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This will also discourage prospective hawkers from putting in excessively high tender bids.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Collectively, our rental policies at NEA-managed hawker centres have served us well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: However, any system will have its pros and cons.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For example, some Opposition Members have suggested that we abandon the tender system to a balloting one or other options.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: While balloting could provide an equal chance to all to obtain a stall at an upfront fixed rate, what balloting could also do is to encourage frivolous applications and excess demand for stalls, especially at popular centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This may not be fair to prospective tenderers with genuine intent to set up a new stall as they see their chances dwindle.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Others have suggested a fixed rent model to keep rental costs under control.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But what price will we use to pre-determine the rent?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Let us say we use the Assessed Market Rate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This low rent helps with their business costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: If we adopt a fixed rent model, then nearly 50% of hawkers will pay much higher rentals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will stay open to consider different models.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In fact, we have tried out price-quality models at SEHCs where the rent is predetermined, and stalls are curated by the operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In summary, when making policies, we must ensure transparency so that bidders can understand easily, while also bringing better outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We continue to monitor the trends closely, as well as the attention that hawker stall rent has attracted recently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: A small percentage of bids can be quite high, especially at popular hawker centres, for example, the recent bid for a cooked food stall at Marine Parade Central Food Centre which exceeded $10,000.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: There may be situations where prospective tenderers put in overly high bids upfront to secure their preferred stall, expecting their rents to be adjusted downwards to Assessed Market Rate after the first three years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I announced last week that we will implement two measures, to encourage more realistic bidding behaviour that better consider actual market conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: First, we will make available more information and online business cost estimation tools.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We are introducing this to assist and encourage tenderers to make a more informed decision and bid realistically.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: However, some tenderers may still choose to submit excessively high bids.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Hence, we will stagger downward adjustment of tendered rent over a longer period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Doing so serves to deter prospective hawkers from submitting unrealistic bids.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Nonetheless, we hope that these changes will work hand in hand to encourage prospective hawkers to bid in a more considered and realistic manner moving forward.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will continue to monitor the tender bidding behaviours closely and review our tenancy policies from time to time to ensure that they stay relevant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: There have been many comments about the SEHC model by Members today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I want to reiterate that regardless of how we manage our hawker centres, whether it is by NEA or operators under our SEHC model, our fundamental principles remain the same.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Hawkers and consumers remain at the heart of our policies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This was with Singaporeans in mind, to meet the community’s rising needs for access to a variety of food options at affordable prices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We also needed to set up our new centres for success.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This meant exploring new models and being open to different approaches that would allow us to achieve our objectives to safeguard hawker livelihoods and consumers’ needs while adapting to an evolving operating context.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In addition, foremost on our minds was to ensure that our new centres would be vibrant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: There was a time when residents were unhappy that hawker centres were not opening long enough to serve their dining needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In fact, this issue was raised before and debated in Parliament too, back in 2010.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In recent years, we have also received feedback from residents and the community about operating hours for hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is the context for developing the SEHC model.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We assessed the SEHC model to have various benefits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: First, SEHC operators possess industry knowledge and experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: They can leverage their expertise in F&B and stall management to ensure the vibrancy of new centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Second, SEHC operators can leverage their F&B networks to curate food mix and support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Third, SEHC operators can introduce new and innovative practices to support stallholders in navigating changing operating contexts and industry developments, such as onboarding onto digital and online ordering platforms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Good curation and visitorship are important ingredients for a vibrant hawker centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These allow hawkers to thrive and earn a fair livelihood, and as a result, a hawker centre can better meet the dining needs of the residents and community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We believe these objectives can be met by the SEHC management model.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As with all models, there will be operational issues that we need to continuously calibrate and make adjustments from time to time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will continue to engage SEHC operators and hawkers to make changes where necessary.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In developing the model, we sought to strike a balance between ensuring patrons’ needs for affordable food options and meals and hawkers' needs for a conducive operating environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We have safeguards in place to ensure that operators do not profiteer and are expected to work closely with NEA as well as hawkers, to consider the interests and needs of both hawkers and residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: When submitting tender proposals, prospective SEHC operators must also include their proposed stall rentals and other operating costs charged to stallholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Second, to ensure fair operating conditions for hawkers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Such conditions are part of the tenancy agreements between the SEHC operators and the stallholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For example, operating hours specify that stallholders must open their stalls for a specific number of days and hours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This serves to ensure that centres would be vibrant and have sufficient stalls in operation to serve meals for residents throughout the day.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Nonetheless, conditions are also in place to take care of the well-being of our hawkers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For instance, on operating hours, stallholders are not required to work more than five days a week or eight hours a day.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These are guidelines that operators need to comply with, and operators are also required to explain the tenancy agreement to stallholders in simple terms for stallholders’ understanding before they sign it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Third, to ensure that operators serve the hawkers and the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Operators have run initiatives to raise footfall and business levels to benefit stallholders, such as providing shuttle bus services at Yishun Park Hawker Centre and organising festive events at Bukit Canberra Hawker Centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Hawkers still retain flexibility to offer other food items and sell them at appropriate prices, so that they can continue to earn an overall fair living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Hawkers are not expected to make a loss selling value meals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: SEHC operators can propose to revise the price of such value meals options, which NEA will review based on the market situation and stallholders’ ability to make a fair livelihood.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: With our efforts over the years, the SEHC model is generally working well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Based on NEA’s recent surveys, over 97% of patrons and stallholders were overall satisfied with SEHCs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Average occupancy at SEHCs remains high with low stall turnover and there continues to be high interest in applying for stalls at new SEHCs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Nonetheless, we do not take all this for granted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We also recognise that some operators have have faced implementation challenges along the way, especially when they first started.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is also why we renew the management of SEHCs via open tender after the incumbent operators’ final tenancy term.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It is a transparent process that allows incumbents that have done well to be considered favourably, while weeding out poorer-performing operators if necessary.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Such a system enables healthy competition between the SEHC operators and motivates them to refine and improve their management models over time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: External circumstances such as inflation have presented challenges for our hawkers and Singaporeans alike, especially in recent years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For hawkers, increases in operating costs, especially for ingredients, can mean having to absorb some of these costs or making the difficult decision to raise prices for customers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For Singaporeans, having to pay 50 cents or a dollar more for hawker meals could feel like a dent in their wallets, as prices of other daily essentials also go up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As Members have mentioned, the Government, with the support of our local community and private sector, are doing what we can to mitigate the impact of these rising costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The core of today's debate is how to ensure our hawker culture continues to thrive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Government will spare no effort in supporting hawkers and the hawker trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We must establish a strong social compact to ensure that hawker culture can flourish.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Hawker centres are our community dining rooms, providing affordable food for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It is because of the efforts of generations of hawkers that Singapore's cuisine has become world-renowned.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: After Singapore's Independence in 1965, resources were invested to gradually relocate street vendors to hawker centres so that hawkers could operate their businesses safely, comfortably and hygienically in a conducive environment, while diners could eat happily with a peace of mind.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: With changing times, the Government has continuously explored different operating models, so that hawker centres can keep pace with the times, adjust to the changing business environment and safeguard hawkers' livelihoods while meeting consumers’ needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Government appreciates hawkers' contributions and understands the various challenges they face, including rising cost pressures and changing consumer needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will also work closely with hawkers and value their feedback.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Here, I want to pay tribute to our hardworking and resilient hawkers!

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: Allow me to first correct a misunderstanding by Senior Minister of State Koh.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: He mentioned that there is an inconsistency in our proposals for rent between mine and Mr Leong Mun Wai's.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: I just want to clarify that there is no inconsistency.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: In my speech, I used the term pre-determined rent, not fixed rent.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: So, pre-determined is either a fixed rent of $500 per month or 3% of gross revenue.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: In my English version, I did not go into the details because it was already covered by Mr Leong.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: But in my Chinese portion, I did mention this.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: I have two clarifications for Senior Minister of State Koh.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: He mentioned that the Government will ensure that the SEHC operators do not profit excessively.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: Can I ask how the Government does that?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: Do you monitor the profitability level of the operators, for example, their return on equity ratios?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: If so, can Senior Minister of State Koh share the data?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: The second clarification is: he mentioned that NEA has guidelines on rental contracts.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: Can I ask whether there is any legal force behind those guidelines?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: What are the consequences if rental contracts deviate from those guidelines?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Sorry, can I have the Member's second question?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ms Poa, do you want to turn on your mic?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: The NEA guidelines on contract terms, whether there is any legal force behind it and what are the consequences for deviating from those guidelines?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: My apologies, Speaker, for prolonging this, but just a few clarifications.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: First, in terms of the point on hiring of foreign workers, I appreciate the Senior Minister of State's point of not ruling it out.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: But I mean, as mentioned in my speech, if we look at, for example, just any other food court that we have, I think foreigners already run stalls.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: So, as an intermediate step, would the Government consider allowing Malaysian work pass holders to work in our hawker centres, because I mean, as HDB policy suggests, Malaysians are already quite culturally similar, so they are exempt from SPR quotas and all of that.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: So, given that this is already being practised by a lot of Government agencies like HDB, Town Council and so on, would it consider a pilot for hawker centres which are particularly notorious for high rents, whether it is Marine Parade or Newton?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: And this will help to mitigate some of the concerns that Senior Minister of State has raised.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: I think my colleague, Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, has also talked about this in the context of HDB coffee shops.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I think on the issue of foreign workers, in my speech, I did say that actually, there is no science to it.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Let us see what this move does and what the effect is first, before we decide whether it is appropriate to make further moves.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The comparison with food courts is not exactly a correct one because there is a difference with hawker centres where we want to preserve the UNESCO heritage.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In a hawker centre, the stallholders themselves operate the stalls.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: That is one of the requirements that they cannot outsource to someone else to manage the stalls.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: They have to tend to the stalls themselves so that they are the ones who ply the trade.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But once we change the model to one in which the stall owners can now hire a certain complement of foreign workers or even local workers for that matter to run the stall instead of themselves, you are then turning it into potentially a franchise model where now the actual operator is not the one cooking.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It is someone else doing the cooking and this person becomes a business owner hiring different workers, local or otherwise, to work across different stalls rather than he himself running the stall with his own special touch, special recipe.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, there is an inherent change in the nature of how hawker centres will become.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I think that is something where we are still trying to make sure we hold fast to the original concept of what a hawker stall and a hawker centre is.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But in time to come, when demographics change, there may well be a need for us to make further moves.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But let us see what the current measures help the hawkers first.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: On PQM, in my speech, I did say that today, in some of our SEHCs already practise PQM.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, it is not something that we are averse to; it is something that we already tried in our SEHCs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But it is easier to be done when there is actually an operator who has a business concept behind it, who has a certain idea how that particular centre is to be run in terms of placemaking and programming, so that, with a price quality matrix, he selects a certain complementary type of stalls to operate in there with a certain business model in mind.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Whereas in the typical NEA-managed hawker centre, which is running through a bidding system, it really is more of a kind of mix that is determined by what the market wants, rather than a placemaker per se trying to curate and decide which stall can run in a hawker centre.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I hope you understand what I am trying to get at with the different models between what the SEHC is and what a typical NEA-managed hawker centre is like.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The third point is about awarding the highest bidder but making him pay the second highest bid.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I think that will make the second highest bidder a bit aggrieved, would it not?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: If you are going to award the second highest bid, then why did I not get it, but you give it to the highest bidder?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Like I said, the vast majority of bids – 44% of them – got the bids below the Assessed Market Rent, which means close to half of the stalls actually pay in the first tenancy term less than the Assessed Market Rent.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And the number of bids that are in that stratospheric range is actually a very small number.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I hope we would not discard a system that has worked well and benefited a large number of hawkers just because of one outlier bid.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But I must also admit that I have never felt that I had that much power over this Chamber before.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I think my speech will be about 15 minutes, a summary in English, and then a summary in Chinese.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: However, I think to summarise my concerns, there are these following issues which I think if the Government does not tackle further, the prospects and livelihoods of our hawkers will not improve that much and will threaten the sustainability of our hawker culture on the long term.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, I hope the Government will continue to consider these four points that I raised.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: And if you take into consideration the possibility of conflict of interest between the private operator and he operating a social enterprise hawker centre, we are of the view that it may be better off for experienced civil servants of the Hawker Centres Group to actually provide more help to the management of the hawker centres.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: That is one of our points and that is why we say, bring the whole thing up as the new Government agency, Hawker Singapore.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Is it not better off to have a system whereby the bidder continues to pay as he bid?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Or after three years, a new bidding again for the same stall.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, we still think that this kind of tender system did contribute to the escalating prices in our HDB coffee shops and food courts.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: And that is one of the major causes of escalating cooked food prices in the long run.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: In doing so, you are putting them at a disadvantage.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: And in order for us to preserve the distinctive Singaporean character of our hawker culture, we must ensure the individual hawkers are competitive vis a vis the corporatised hawkers.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: If you disallow that to the individual hawkers, then you continue to make them the underdogs.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: And my last point, you may have a lot of competing objectives, but to impose budget meals and discounts to hawker meals, imposing the cost on the hawkers is an objective that you can do without.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Those are the main points that I would like to say.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I regard our local hawkers as another group of workers essential to the functioning of our society that really need our attention.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Exemplified by many of my Chinatown neighbours in the past, our Pioneer hawkers started off as humble folks who just want to earn enough to feed their families.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: They worked very hard but are satisfied with getting meagre profits.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: As a result, we were able to enjoy cheap and good hawker food for a long time.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Today, in the 21st century, hawkers are facing tremendous headwinds, with high rental, shortage of manpower, unfair competition and increasing constraints from corporatisation, and also the persistent societal expectations to provide cheap and good food.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: At the rate we are going, our traditional hawker culture which is based on the hard work and enterprise of individual hawkers will slowly wither away.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Corporatisation of the hawker trade is a natural development of the market economy, but we can ensure a more level playing field for our individual hawkers to thrive and flourish.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The current pride of our hawkers is at least partly due to the policies by the Government.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The onus is now on the Government to consider our suggestions to provide better support for hawkers in the future.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, PSP has put forward a Motion to protect our hawker culture, calling on the Government to review policies related to hawkers and hawker centre management, and to provide better support for hawkers to maintain and develop Singapore's hawker culture.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The hawker culture is not only a part of Singaporean identity but also a UNESCO intangible cultural heritage.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Hawker centres, as "people's kitchens", provide Singaporeans with delicious and affordable food, offering a buffer against high living costs.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: At the same time, the hawker industry provides an ideal entrepreneurial platform for young, aspiring business owners.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Promoting hawker food domestically and internationally, winning over hearts and palates worldwide, is a way for Singapore to enhance its soft power, which will bring significant economic benefits.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Therefore, PSP believes that protecting and preserving hawker culture is crucial.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: However, the challenges faced by hawkers are threatening the survival of this unique culture.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Thus, PSP calls on the Government to re-examine its policies.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: In today's Motion, PSP has put forward six policy recommendations, which my colleague Hazel Poa has also introduced in Chinese in her speech.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Our local hawkers are another crucial group maintaining societal operations, equally deserving of our attention.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: In today's debate, PSP has put forward some policy recommendations, hoping to spark more public discussion and help create more space to maintain and develop our hawker culture.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: We hope the Government will consider our suggestions and let Singaporeans judge which policy proposals are more beneficial for Singapore in the long run.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I hope everyone in Parliament agrees that hawker centres and hawkers must thrive so that we can continue to enjoy delicious and affordable hawker food, and maintain and develop our country's unique hawker culture. : Sir, having made my points clear, the PSP is ready to support the amended Motion, which is not too different from the original Motion tabled by me.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: This is to show that this House is united in our support for hawkers.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: After five-and-a-half hours of debate, any clarifications for Mr Leong?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I am glad to say that we have now come to the conclusion of the debate.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I did not hear any Noes, but is there anyone who wants to record their dissent?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The original Motion as amended is now before the House.
